purpose: How a home-security dealer decides between authorized-dealer programs and the independent model, funds the creation of each monitored account (equipment subsidy versus margin, the wholesale-retail monitoring spread, sell-versus-hold, holdback and chargeback exposure), selects territory and customer segments, and builds a lead engine and disclosure-first in-home sales practice — treating every commission, multiple, rate and holdback as a per-contract mechanism to verify, never an assumed figure.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

every dollar figure, commission rate, account multiple, holdback percentage and monitoring rate is a per-deal contract fact; this KB teaches the mechanisms that produce those numbers and how to verify each in the governing agreement, and never asserts values
the operator sells defensive, lawful security only: systems that prevent, detect and alarm intrusions for a customer who lawfully controls the protected premises

sales-side legal obligations (solicitation permits, cooling-off rights, contract disclosure and auto-renewal rules, telemarketing restrictions) vary by state and city and must be verified in the operating jurisdiction before any channel or contract goes live
content is educational and operational knowledge for the dealer-operator, not personalized financial, legal, tax or insurance advice for any specific person or deal
exclusions: site survey and risk walk-through, panel/sensor/doorbell/camera package design, installation quality and testing, install permits, false-alarm ordinances, low-voltage licensing execution, and subcontract-versus-in-house install trade-offs — the system-design-and-installation KB owns these

central-station versus self/cloud monitoring stack choice, building RMR through monitoring, cloud video and service plans, attrition drivers and the retention playbook, renewal-time contract hygiene, and valuation of a seasoned monitored-account book — the monitoring-RMR-and-retention KB owns these

offensive, covert or unlawful surveillance uses of security equipment; the business exists to prevent, detect and alarm intrusions, and requests outside that defensive scope are declined, not designed around

asserting specific commissions, prices, account multiples, holdback percentages, monitoring rates or market sizes as fact — economics appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands verified per deal against the signed agreement
asserting jurisdiction-specific licensing, permit, cooling-off or contract-disclosure rules — obligation classes are named with an explicit verify-locally flag
personalized financial, legal, tax or insurance advice to the dealer or to any customer

competency_questions.question: What does an alarm dealership actually sell, and where does the money come from when one monitored account is created?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEALER_BUSINESS_THESIS frames the monitored account as the unit of value with its three revenue components, and ACCOUNT_UNIT_ECONOMICS shows how creation cost is computed and recovered

competency_questions.question: Should I sign with an authorized-dealer program or run independent, and what actually changes under each model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_MODEL_CHOICE compares account ownership, brand access, funding, obligations and exit consequences and states the decision criteria

competency_questions.question: Which terms must be extracted and verified from a dealer-program agreement before signing, and why can none of them be assumed from industry folklore?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEALER_AGREEMENT_DILIGENCE names the economic and control clauses to extract (purchase terms, holdback, chargeback window, quotas, territory, exit) and HOLDBACK_CHARGEBACK_MECHANICS explains the guarantee mechanics those clauses create

competency_questions.question: How is the true cost of creating one monitored account computed, and through which paths is that cost recovered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_UNIT_ECONOMICS gives the creation-cost mechanism (marketing + commission + subsidized equipment + install labor minus upfront fees) and MONITORING_SPREAD_MECHANICS explains the recurring recovery path

competency_questions.question: When does subsidizing the equipment beat charging full hardware margin, and what new exposures does a deep subsidy create?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EQUIPMENT_SUBSIDY_VS_MARGIN states the trade-off and its coupling to term length and chargeback exposure, and CONTRACT_TERM_DESIGN shows the honest-term limits on subsidy recovery

competency_questions.question: How do holdbacks and chargebacks actually work, and which sales-side behaviors control that exposure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOLDBACK_CHARGEBACK_MECHANICS explains withheld funding and clawback windows as agreement mechanisms and CUSTOMER_CREDIT_QUALITY_GATE shows how point-of-sale qualification controls the exposure

competency_questions.question: How do I decide whether to sell a newly created account for cash or hold it for the monitoring spread?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELL_VS_HOLD_DECISION states the cash-now versus annuity trade-off with the factors that move an account multiple, and FUNDING_TIMELINE_CASHFLOW ties the decision to the creation engine's cash needs

competency_questions.question: How do I choose a territory and target segments so that accounts are cheaper to create and better quality when created?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERRITORY_SELECTION covers density, saturation and program territory rights and SEGMENT_TARGETING covers homeowner/renter/light-commercial fit signals with qualification criteria

competency_questions.question: Which lead channels should feed the funnel, and how is each channel judged beyond its cost per lead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAD_ENGINE_DESIGN scores channels on cost-per-funded-account and downstream cancellation behavior, not raw lead price, and names the compliance check each channel needs

competency_questions.question: What does an ethical in-home security consultation look like — including with an elderly or vulnerable prospect — and where is the hard line on fear-selling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ETHICAL_SELLING_CODE states the disclosure-first, no-fear-selling and vulnerable-consumer rules as binding constraints and INHOME_SALES_PROCESS shows the consultation sequence that operationalizes them

competency_questions.question: How should sales-rep compensation be structured so the incentive plan does not manufacture the very accounts that charge back?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALES_COMP_PLAN explains vesting against the chargeback window and clawback on confirmed misrepresentation as the alignment mechanisms

competency_questions.question: What must be true of an account before it is funded, sold, or handed to the monitoring book?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_PACKAGE_ASSEMBLY lists the fundable-package contents and CREATION_QUALITY_GATE states the definition-of-done that blocks a defective account from funding or handoff

competency_questions.question: Which legal and consumer-protection obligation classes touch alarm selling, and how are they handled without asserting local specifics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_PERIMETER names the sales-side obligation classes with a verify-locally flag on each and CONTRACT_TERM_DESIGN shows where disclosure duties land in the contract

glossary.definition: The monthly amount a monitored account pays for monitoring and attached services; the industry's pricing unit — accounts and books are quoted as multiples of RMR, so every economic conversation reduces to how much RMR an account carries and how durable it is.

The convention of pricing a monitored account as some multiple of its RMR when it is sold or funded; the multiple is set by the governing agreement and moves with contract term remaining, rate level, customer credit tier and the seller's historical attrition — it is verified per deal, never assumed from hearsay.

The portion of an account's purchase or funding price that a program or buyer withholds for a guarantee period against early cancellation, released on the schedule the agreement states if the account stays alive and paying.

The clawback of previously paid funding (or its offset against the holdback) when an account cancels, defaults or is found misrepresented within the agreement's guarantee window; the mechanism that transmits early-cancellation risk back to whoever created the account.

Selling the alarm system below cost or heavily discounted to win the monitoring relationship, with the shortfall recovered over the monitoring term; the deeper the subsidy, the more the dealer has effectively lent the customer against their future payments.

The all-in cash consumed to create one funded monitored account: marketing cost per closed sale plus sales compensation plus the unrecovered equipment and install labor, minus whatever upfront fees the customer paid; the number every funding and pacing decision keys off.

The difference between the retail monitoring rate the customer pays and the wholesale cost the dealer pays for monitoring service; the recurring gross margin per held account and the annuity a dealer forfeits when an account is sold.

A brand's channel arrangement in which a dealer sells and installs under the brand's name and the program funds or purchases the accounts created, in exchange for quotas, pricing rules, territory terms, holdbacks and account-flow obligations set in the dealer agreement.

A consumer-protection obligation class giving buyers in home-solicitation sales a statutory window to cancel without penalty; the window's length and notice formalities are jurisdiction-specific and must be verified locally before contracts and scripts are finalized.

A pre-funding recorded confirmation, made after the sale and usually after activation, that the customer understands the price, term, cancellation terms and what was installed; programs use it to catch misrepresentation before money moves, and good dealers use it as their own quality gate.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for alarm_dealer_program_and_account_economics work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix what the business actually is: a machine that creates monitored accounts. Each sale produces three revenue components — equipment margin (often deliberately sacrificed), an installation fee, and a recurring monitoring relationship — and the recurring component is the asset: a funded account either throws off a monthly spread for years or converts to cash at a multiple of its RMR. Every downstream choice (program versus independent, subsidy depth, channel mix, comp design) is judged by one question: what does it do to the cost of creating an account and to the value and survival of the account created?

included: the three revenue components at sale
account-as-asset framing
creation-cost versus account-value lens for all decisions
excluded: designing the system itself
operating the monitoring book after handoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the dealer's realized economics show the recurring component is no longer the dominant value driver

pros.claim: Judging every decision by cost-to-create versus value-created stops the dealership from optimizing hardware profit while starving the asset that actually compounds
pros.example: a dealer who prices installs for maximum margin closes fewer monitoring relationships than one who treats hardware as the door to the account

cons.claim: The account-machine frame can seduce an operator into counting signed contracts as value before the accounts survive their first year
cons.example: celebrating a record month of installs that later cancels out through the chargeback window

failure_modes: running the business as an equipment retailer and treating monitoring as an afterthought
counting created accounts as realized value before funding and the guarantee window clear
acceptance_tests: the operating thesis names all three revenue components, states the account as the unit of value, and defines both recovery paths (held spread, sale at a multiple) as mechanisms
revisit_triggers: the recurring component's economics shift industry-wide (wholesale monitoring cost, funding appetite)
the dealer's own mix of held versus sold accounts changes strategy

nodes.definition: Decide the structural question first: create accounts inside an authorized-dealer program or as an independent dealer. A program supplies a national brand, sales infrastructure, financing of account creation and a built-in account buyer — in exchange for quotas, pricing rules, mandatory account flow, territory constraints and exit clauses that can leave the dealer with neither book nor customers. Independence keeps account ownership, monitoring-stack freedom and the whole spread, but the dealer self-funds creation, builds their own brand trust at the door, and must find their own capital or buyers. The choice is a capital-and-control decision: who funds account creation, who owns what is created, and what happens at exit.

included: ownership, funding, obligation and exit comparison
decision criteria by capital position and strategic goal
hybrid and transition paths between models
excluded: clause-level reading of a specific agreement
monitoring-stack selection

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a program term amendment or a capital event changes which model the comparison favors

pros.claim: A program lets a thin-capital dealer create accounts at a pace their own balance sheet could never fund
pros.example: a two-person startup installing daily because the program purchases each account days after activation instead of the dealer waiting years for spread recovery

cons.claim: Program obligations reach far beyond economics into what the dealer may sell, where, and what remains theirs at exit
cons.example: a dealer discovering at termination that accounts they created belong to the program and a non-solicit bars them from their own former customers

failure_modes: choosing the model on the headline account price while ignoring ownership and exit clauses
going independent without the capital to survive the years-long spread-recovery cycle
acceptance_tests: the decision memo compares both models on account ownership, creation funding, obligations (quota, pricing, flow), and exit outcome, and records why the chosen model fits the dealer's capital and goal
revisit_triggers: the dealer's capital position changes enough to make the other model viable
the program materially amends quotas, funding terms or territory rights

nodes.definition: Read the dealer agreement as the source of truth for every number the business will run on, before signing and again at every amendment. Extract into a term sheet: the account purchase price mechanism (multiple basis and the RMR definition it applies to), holdback percentage and release schedule, chargeback window and triggering events, minimum production quotas and their penalties, equipment and pricing rules, territory scope and exclusivity, brand-use rules, and — hardest-hitting — termination and exit clauses: who owns created accounts, what non-solicitation survives, and what happens to unreleased holdback. Industry folklore about typical multiples or windows is a hypothesis, never an input; only the signed document's terms enter the economic model.

included: clause extraction into a working term sheet
economic terms as per-contract facts
exit and ownership consequence analysis
excluded: negotiating posture beyond flagging onerous terms
legal advice on enforceability — that goes to counsel

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an amendment, a funding discrepancy, or counsel's reading changes an extracted term

pros.claim: A written term sheet extracted from the actual agreement makes every later model and decision auditable back to a clause
pros.example: when a funding payment arrives short, the term sheet shows in seconds whether the holdback schedule or a chargeback explains it

cons.claim: Diligence takes time and legal spend exactly when the dealer is eager to start producing
cons.example: a counsel review of exit clauses delaying signing while a competing dealer starts knocking the same streets

failure_modes: signing on the headline multiple without reading the chargeback and exit clauses
running the account model on remembered folklore numbers instead of the contract's actual terms
acceptance_tests: a term sheet exists listing purchase-price mechanism, holdback and release schedule, chargeback window and triggers, quotas, territory, brand rules, and exit/ownership clauses, each traceable to a clause reference in the signed document
revisit_triggers: the program issues an amendment or a new agreement version
a funding statement disagrees with the term sheet's predictions

nodes.definition: Bind the whole sales operation to a written code that is enforced ahead of any quota: security is sold on honest risk information and system capability, never on manufactured fear — no invented neighborhood-crime claims, no staged urgency, no implying the customer is in danger tonight if they do not sign. Disclosure comes first: total of payments, term length, auto-renewal behavior and cancellation rights are stated plainly before a signature is requested. Vulnerable consumers get extra protection, not extra pressure: when an elderly or confused prospect shows signs of not tracking the terms, the close stops, a family member or trusted third party is invited in, and the sale reschedules or dies. The code also draws the lawful-scope line: the dealer sells defensive intrusion prevention, detection and alarm — requests for covert or unlawful surveillance are declined.

included: no-fear-selling rule with concrete banned tactics
disclosure-before-signature sequence
vulnerable-consumer stop-and-slow protocol
defensive-lawful-scope line
excluded: the consultation script mechanics
jurisdiction-specific statutes — named as classes in the regulatory perimeter

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint pattern, audit finding or regulator inquiry shows the code is not holding in the field

pros.claim: A written, enforced code converts ethics from a rep's personal judgment into an operating standard that survives hiring and quota pressure
pros.example: a top producer's staged 'there were break-ins on this street' opener gets the same script audit and consequence as a rookie's

cons.claim: The code slows and sometimes kills closes that pressure tactics would have won
cons.example: an elderly homeowner's rescheduled close never completes because the family talks her out of it

failure_modes: treating the code as marketing while tolerating fear scripts that hit quota
letting a vulnerable prospect sign a multi-year term they visibly do not understand
acceptance_tests: the code names banned tactics (invented crime claims, staged urgency, hidden terms), requires disclosure of price/term/renewal/cancellation before signature, and contains a stop-and-involve-a-third-party protocol for vulnerable prospects
every rep has signed the code and script audits check compliance against it
revisit_triggers: a complaint, cancellation cluster or regulator contact implicates a sales practice
a new channel or script is introduced

nodes.definition: Map the classes of legal obligation that touch alarm selling and pin a verify-locally flag on each, because the specifics differ by state and city and change over time: alarm-sales or salesperson registration classes; door-to-door solicitation permits and do-not-knock registries; home-solicitation cooling-off rights and their notice formalities; contract-disclosure and auto-renewal statutes; telemarketing and do-not-call restrictions for phone outreach. The node's discipline is procedural, not encyclopedic: before any channel, script or contract goes live in a jurisdiction, the current local rules for each class are checked and the check is documented. This node covers the selling side only — install permits, false-alarm ordinances and low-voltage licensing live with the installation KB.

included: sales-side obligation classes
per-jurisdiction verification procedure and its documentation
change monitoring for rules already verified
excluded: install permits, false-alarm ordinances, trade licensing — the installation KB
asserting any jurisdiction's current specifics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a jurisdiction entry, rule change or enforcement action touches any obligation class

pros.claim: Naming obligation classes with a verification procedure scales across jurisdictions without ever asserting stale specifics
pros.example: expansion into a neighboring city triggers the same checklist run instead of a guess that the old city's door-permit rule carries over

cons.claim: Class-level knowledge cannot answer a concrete compliance question by itself; someone still has to do the local lookup
cons.example: the checklist says cooling-off rules exist but only the state's current statute says how many days and what notice form

failure_modes: canvassing a city without checking its solicitation-permit and do-not-knock rules
copying contract disclosure language across state lines unverified
acceptance_tests: every active jurisdiction has a documented, dated verification record covering each obligation class before its channels or contracts went live
revisit_triggers: entry into a new city or state
a rule change alert or a complaint referencing a sales-practice statute

nodes.definition: Build the per-account economic model every pricing and pacing decision runs on. Creation cost is a mechanism, not a constant: marketing cost per closed sale (channel spend divided by funded accounts it produced) plus sales compensation plus the unrecovered slice of equipment and install labor, minus upfront fees collected at sale. Recovery has exactly two paths and the model prices both: hold the account and recover through the monthly monitoring spread over the survival horizon, or sell it and recover through the purchase price the agreement's multiple mechanism yields, net of holdback at risk. The model's inputs are per-deal facts — this month's channel spend, this agreement's multiple, this customer's upfront fee — never remembered industry averages, and its output drives subsidy depth, channel pruning and the sell/hold mix.

included: creation-cost mechanism with named per-deal inputs
both recovery paths priced side by side
sensitivity of the model to subsidy, channel and comp choices
excluded: asserting any typical cost or multiple as a number
book-level valuation of seasoned accounts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a realized-versus-modeled variance or an input change forces re-derivation of creation cost

pros.claim: A live per-account model exposes which lever actually moves the business when intuition says otherwise
pros.example: the model showing that trimming drive time via territory density cuts creation cost more than renegotiating equipment pricing ever could

cons.claim: The model is only as honest as its cost attribution, and marketing and labor costs are easy to under-allocate
cons.example: leaving the owner's own unpaid selling hours out of creation cost and concluding accounts are cheaper than they are

failure_modes: running on invented industry-average constants instead of the dealer's own inputs
excluding failed sales and cancelled installs from the marketing cost denominator
acceptance_tests: the worksheet computes creation cost from the dealer's actual channel spend, comp, equipment/labor and fee inputs, and prices both recovery paths using only terms traceable to the governing agreement
revisit_triggers: any input class shifts materially (channel costs, comp plan, equipment pricing, agreement terms)
realized funding or spread outcomes diverge from the model's predictions

nodes.definition: Set the subsidy dial deliberately. Charging full equipment and install margin makes each sale self-funding but prices the offer against every competitor waving a low-entry system; subsidizing — discounting hardware down to or below cost to win the monitoring relationship — buys accounts faster but converts each sale into a loan the customer repays only by staying through the term. The mechanism to hold onto: subsidy depth raises creation cost, lengthens the payback horizon on held accounts, raises the stakes on every early cancellation, and pressures the contract toward longer terms — so the dial is set from the account model and the cash runway, not from what the loudest competitor advertises, and any 'free system' language is only used when the offer genuinely carries no recovery obligation the customer must be told about.

included: the subsidy-depth decision and its coupling to term, cash and chargeback exposure
honest presentation limits on subsidized offers
segment- and channel-specific subsidy variation
excluded: designing the hardware package itself
asserting typical subsidy amounts as figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: subsidized-cohort survival or cash-conversion data contradicts the current dial setting

pros.claim: A calibrated subsidy removes the price objection that blocks monitoring relationships the spread would comfortably repay
pros.example: a starter sensor package offered at install-fee-only turning price-shopping households into funded accounts the full-margin quote kept losing

cons.claim: Every dollar of subsidy is recovered only if the account survives, so deep subsidy concentrates the dealer's capital in its most cancellable asset
cons.example: a heavily subsidized cluster of accounts cancelling in month three and leaving equipment on walls the dealer effectively paid for

failure_modes: matching a competitor's giveaway offer without re-running creation cost and cash pacing
advertising 'free' while burying a recovery obligation in the term
acceptance_tests: each active offer's subsidy depth is justified in the account model with its payback horizon and chargeback exposure stated, and no offer uses 'free' language while carrying an undisclosed recovery obligation
revisit_triggers: cash runway tightens or funding terms change
early-cancellation rates rise on subsidized offers

nodes.definition: Understand the spread that makes a held account an annuity: the customer pays a retail monitoring rate; the dealer pays a wholesale cost for monitoring service (to a central station directly, or embedded in a program's terms); the difference, net of the dealer's own service burden, is recurring gross margin per account per month. What moves each side is mechanism knowledge: wholesale cost moves with account volume, contract commitments and which services ride the account; retail rate moves with the offer architecture, segment and competitive posture; and the spread only materializes across the months the account survives. At creation time this node prices the hold path — how many months of spread repay this account's creation cost — while the operational choice of monitoring stack and the retention work that determines survival belong to the monitoring-and-retention KB.

included: spread as the hold-path recovery mechanism
what moves wholesale and retail sides
months-to-payback framing at creation
excluded: choosing the monitoring stack
retention operations that lengthen survival
asserting typical rates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a wholesale-cost, retail-rate or service-burden change re-prices the hold path

pros.claim: Pricing the hold path in months-to-payback makes sell/hold and subsidy decisions comparable on one axis
pros.example: seeing instantly that a deeper subsidy pushes payback past the term length, meaning the hold path cannot recover it within the guaranteed window

cons.claim: Spread projections flatter the hold path because they assume survival that retention work has not yet earned
cons.example: a payback calculation that looks comfortable until real attrition shortens the average revenue horizon

failure_modes: comparing sell versus hold using gross spread while ignoring the dealer's own service cost per account
treating the projected spread as bankable before the account demonstrates survival
acceptance_tests: the hold-path calculation nets the dealer's service burden out of the spread and states months-to-payback against the account's actual creation cost
revisit_triggers: wholesale terms, retail rates or the service burden change
observed survival diverges from the horizon the spread projection assumed

nodes.definition: Decide, as a standing policy revisited with cash position, what fraction of newly created accounts to sell and what fraction to hold. Selling converts an account into immediate cash at the agreement's multiple mechanism — funding the next round of creation — but forfeits the spread annuity and usually leaves a holdback at risk; holding builds the compounding asset but ties up the creation cost for the whole payback horizon. The decision inputs are mechanical: current cash runway, the modeled months-to-payback on held accounts, the net-of-holdback proceeds the multiple yields on this agreement, and what actually moves a quoted multiple (contract term remaining, rate level, customer credit tier, the dealer's attrition record, paperwork quality). This node owns the creation-time funding decision; valuing and marketing a seasoned book years later belongs to the retention KB.

included: the standing sell/hold mix policy and its inputs
what moves a quoted multiple as mechanism
net-of-holdback proceeds comparison against the hold path
excluded: seasoned-book valuation and sale
asserting any typical multiple

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cash event, funding-term change or attrition shift moves the optimal mix

pros.claim: A standing policy driven by cash and payback math prevents panic sales at whatever multiple is offered when payroll looms
pros.example: a pre-set rule to sell a fixed tranche monthly keeping the dealer out of a distressed single-buyer negotiation

cons.claim: Any fixed mix leaves value on the table in hindsight whenever conditions move
cons.example: a heavy-sell quarter followed by funding terms improving, meaning the sold tranche went at the worse price

failure_modes: selling everything reflexively and never building an owned asset
holding everything on projected spread while creation starves for cash
acceptance_tests: the current mix policy is written down with its cash-runway trigger points, and each tranche sale's proceeds are computed net of holdback from the agreement's actual terms before commitment
revisit_triggers: cash runway crosses a policy trigger
the agreement's multiple mechanism, holdback terms or the dealer's attrition record change

nodes.definition: Master the guarantee machinery that makes funded money provisional. When a program or buyer funds an account, the agreement typically withholds a slice of the price (the holdback) for a defined guarantee period and reserves the right to charge back — claw back funding or offset it against the holdback — if the account cancels, stops paying or proves misrepresented within the window. The mechanics to extract per agreement: the holdback fraction and its release schedule, the window length, which events trigger a chargeback and at what value (full price, declining schedule, RMR-based), and whether replacement accounts can cure. The operational insight is that chargeback exposure is manufactured at the point of sale — by channel quality, script honesty, credit screening and expectation-setting — months before the cancellation that triggers it, so the ledger of at-risk funding must be tracked forward, not discovered on a short funding statement.

included: holdback and release mechanics
chargeback triggers, valuation and cure provisions per agreement
a forward ledger of funding at risk
tracing exposure back to sale-time causes
excluded: the retention work that prevents later-life cancellation
asserting typical holdback percentages or window lengths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a guarantee-term amendment or a chargeback cluster changes the exposure picture

pros.claim: A forward at-risk ledger turns chargebacks from monthly surprises into a managed exposure with named causes
pros.example: the ledger showing one lead channel's accounts carrying most of the at-risk balance two months before the chargebacks land

cons.claim: Guarantee mechanics can push a dealer toward defensive over-tightening that strangles honest volume
cons.example: declining every marginal-credit applicant outright instead of adjusting the offer structure the agreement allows

failure_modes: booking funded amounts as final revenue and being blindsided by clawbacks
fighting chargebacks case by case while leaving the sale-time causes unfixed
acceptance_tests: an at-risk ledger exists tying every funded account to its holdback balance, window expiry and chargeback valuation basis from the agreement, and chargeback post-mortems attribute each event to a sale-time cause category
revisit_triggers: the agreement's guarantee terms change
the at-risk ledger's concentration shifts toward a channel, rep or offer

nodes.definition: Qualify the customer before the account exists, because account quality is decided at the kitchen table, not discovered later. The gate runs consented credit screening where the funding mechanism requires it (programs commonly tier purchase prices by credit band and refuse funding below a floor), confirms the customer's authority over the premises and ability to sustain the monthly payment, and checks intent honestly — a customer signing only to end the conversation is a certain cancellation. The ethics rail is explicit: a declined applicant is declined with dignity and, where it genuinely fits, offered a smaller unsubsidized configuration; the gate never routes marginal applicants into predatory financing workarounds or misstates their information to squeeze past a funding floor — falsified applications are both a fraud exposure and a guaranteed chargeback.

included: consented credit screening tied to the funding mechanism
premises-authority and payment-capacity checks
decline-with-dignity and honest-alternative practice
excluded: the program's own underwriting decision
long-run payment-behavior management on the book

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: funding-tier changes or misclassified cancellations show the gate is mis-calibrated

pros.claim: Screening before install spends a few minutes to avoid the truck roll, equipment loss and clawback of a doomed account
pros.example: a failed credit check at the table converting into a small paid-in-full package instead of a subsidized install that would cancel unpaid

cons.claim: A hard gate turns away some households who would have paid reliably despite a thin file
cons.example: a long-tenured renter with no credit history declined for a subsidized package they could have carried

failure_modes: installing before qualification and eating the reversal
massaging application data to clear a funding floor
acceptance_tests: no install is scheduled before the qualification record (consent, credit outcome where required, premises authority, payment capacity) is complete, and declined applicants are logged with the honest-alternative outcome
revisit_triggers: the funding mechanism's credit tiers or floor change
cancellation post-mortems show qualified accounts failing for a reason the gate misses

nodes.definition: Structure the customer-facing monitoring agreement at the point of sale so it recovers the economics without burying the customer: term length set to what subsidy recovery honestly requires rather than the longest term a form allows; the total of payments, monthly rate, term, auto-renewal behavior and cancellation mechanics stated in plain language and walked through before signature; cooling-off notice included in the form the jurisdiction's rules require (verify locally); and early-termination provisions that are a fair recovery of real unrecovered cost, not a punitive trap. Alarm contracts are consumer-protection sensitive precisely because the industry's worst actors hid auto-renewals and evergreen terms — this node treats honest terms as an economic asset: accounts that understood what they signed cancel less, complain less, and survive funding verification. Renewal-time practice on aged accounts belongs to the retention KB.

included: term-length architecture tied to subsidy recovery
plain-language disclosure of price, term, renewal and cancellation before signature
fair early-termination design
cooling-off formality inclusion per verified local rules
excluded: renewal-time contract hygiene on the aged book
asserting any jurisdiction's disclosure statute specifics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rule change, complaint pattern or funding rejection traces to a contract term or its disclosure

pros.claim: Plain, walked-through terms are cheap insurance against the cancellations, chargebacks and complaints that hidden terms breed
pros.example: a customer who initialed the auto-renewal line after having it explained not becoming the year-three regulator complaint that a buried clause produces

cons.claim: Honest terms and shorter feasible commitments can price the dealer out of deals a hidden-term competitor still closes
cons.example: losing a price-led household to a rival whose lower monthly hides a longer evergreen renewal

failure_modes: stretching term length to cover a subsidy the offer should not have carried
using a stale contract form whose disclosure formalities no longer match the jurisdiction's current rules
acceptance_tests: every contract form in use states total of payments, term, renewal behavior and cancellation mechanics in plain language, carries the jurisdiction-verified cooling-off formalities, and its early-termination charge traces to real unrecovered cost
revisit_triggers: a disclosure-rule change in any active jurisdiction
cancellation or complaint patterns implicating a contract term

nodes.definition: Choose where to create accounts as an economic decision, not a map preference. Density is the quiet cost lever: clustered customers cut drive time per install and service call, let one canvassing pass cover more doors, and make neighbor referrals compound — the same crew creates more accounts per week in one tight area than scattered across a metro. Against density weigh saturation: a territory thick with competitors' yard signs and recently knocked doors raises acquisition cost and lowers close rates. And under a dealer program, territory is also a contract fact: exclusivity or scope clauses in the agreement can bar or protect specific areas, so the map is drawn inside the agreement's lines. Signals worth reading per candidate area: housing tenure and turnover, new-construction activity, existing-competitor presence, and the practical radius the install crew can serve without motel nights.

included: density economics of clustered accounts
saturation reading per candidate area
program territory rights as binding map lines
serviceable-radius realism
excluded: segment-level targeting inside the chosen area
install-crew scheduling mechanics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: territory performance data or agreement territory terms shift the map

pros.claim: Clustering compresses the two costs the account model is most sensitive to: drive time and marketing reach per funded account
pros.example: three installs on one street in one afternoon versus three installs across three towns in three days on the same payroll

cons.claim: Committing to a tight territory concentrates exposure to its local shocks
cons.example: a dominant local employer's layoff wave hitting cancellation rates across the whole clustered book at once

failure_modes: chasing any willing buyer anywhere and letting windshield time eat the account model
canvassing into an area the dealer agreement assigns to another dealer
acceptance_tests: the chosen territory is documented with its density rationale, saturation read, agreement-rights check and serviceable radius before channels launch into it
revisit_triggers: close rates or per-account costs drift in the current territory
the agreement's territory terms change or a competitor saturates the area

nodes.definition: Inside the territory, aim the machine at segments whose accounts are creatable and durable. Established homeowners are the core: premises authority is clean, tenure predicts survival, and equity in the home correlates with staying through a term. New movers are the highest-intent window — security is bought in the first weeks after a move more than any other time — reachable through realtor and builder relationships rather than invented urgency. Renters need honest special handling: landlord consent for anything attached, portable or shorter-commitment configurations, and no multi-year term sold against a twelve-month lease. Light-commercial storefronts (the shop row, the small office) are a legitimate adjacent segment with different hours, contacts and contract counterparties — worth taking deliberately, not accidentally. Each chosen segment gets explicit qualification criteria and its own fit between offer structure, term and expected tenure.

included: segment choice and qualification criteria
mover-window and referral-alliance logic
renter and light-commercial special handling
offer-to-tenure fit per segment
excluded: the lead channels that reach each segment
designing the physical package per premises

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: segment-level conversion or survival data reorders which segments deserve the machine's attention

pros.claim: Aiming at the mover window buys intent instead of manufacturing it, which both converts better and sells cleaner
pros.example: a realtor-referred family closing on a straightforward walkthrough where a cold door knock would have needed pressure to create urgency

cons.claim: Narrow segment focus leaves demand on the table and can overfit the offer to one household profile
cons.example: a homeowner-tuned pitch and term structure failing awkwardly in a renter-heavy neighborhood the territory includes

failure_modes: selling homeowner terms to renters and manufacturing predictable cancellations
drifting into light-commercial accounts without adjusting contracts and contacts
acceptance_tests: each active segment has written qualification criteria and an offer-and-term structure matched to its expected tenure, including landlord-consent handling for renters
revisit_triggers: segment-level survival or close-rate data diverges
the territory's composition shifts (new construction, rental conversion)

nodes.definition: Build the lead engine as a portfolio of channels, each scored on what it costs per funded account and how its accounts behave afterward — never on raw cost per lead. The working channels: customer and neighbor referrals (cheapest and best-surviving, engineered through visible yard signs, referral asks and neighborhood presence after each install); alliances with realtors, insurance agents, builders and property managers who meet the mover window naturally; door canvassing, which works in dense territory but is the most regulated and reputation-exposed channel and runs only inside verified local solicitation rules; local digital presence harvesting in-market search; and purchased leads, bought only with tracked downstream quality since aggregated leads routinely produce accounts that fail funding or cancel early. Every channel carries two ledgers — its per-funded-account cost feeding the account model, and its accounts' cancellation and chargeback record feeding channel pruning.

included: channel portfolio design and per-channel compliance checks
cost-per-funded-account scoring
downstream quality tracking per channel
referral-loop engineering
excluded: the in-home conversation itself
asserting typical per-lead prices

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: channel-level funded-cost or downstream-quality data reorders the portfolio

pros.claim: Scoring channels on funded-account cost and survival reallocates spend toward the accounts that actually stick
pros.example: referral and realtor channels beating a cheap purchased-lead source once early cancellations are counted against it

cons.claim: Quality-scored channel management needs attribution discipline small dealers often lack
cons.example: walk-in and referral credit tangled together until no channel's true cost is knowable

failure_modes: buying lead volume on price and discovering the quality in the chargeback ledger
canvassing a jurisdiction before its solicitation rules are verified
acceptance_tests: every active channel has a documented compliance check for its jurisdiction and a running cost-per-funded-account and downstream-quality record that channel decisions cite
revisit_triggers: a channel's downstream quality or cost drifts
a solicitation-rule change touches an active channel

nodes.definition: Run the in-home consultation as a structured, honest sequence: open by understanding the household — who lives there, entry points that worry them, what prompted the appointment — without editorializing fear onto their answers; walk the home at needs level (which doors, which floor, pets, elderly parents) while leaving the technical site survey and package engineering to the design-and-install discipline; present a configuration and quote with the subsidy, monthly rate, term, renewal and cancellation terms stated before any close is attempted; and close without manufactured urgency — a same-visit signature is welcome, but a prospect who wants a day to think gets it, because a customer argued into a contract becomes a cancellation with extra steps. The signed pack always includes the disclosures the ethics code and the jurisdiction's verified rules require, and the rep records what was promised so the welcome call can verify against it.

included: consultation sequence from discovery to disclosed close
needs-level home walkthrough framing
promise recording for later verification
no-pressure close discipline
excluded: technical site survey and package design — the installation KB
the credit screening mechanics that follow the close

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verification mismatches, cancellation reasons or rule changes implicate the consultation sequence

pros.claim: A disclosed, unpressured close produces accounts that survive verification and the guarantee window because the customer got what they understood they bought
pros.example: a welcome call breezing through confirmation because the rep's recorded promises match the contract line by line

cons.claim: Structured honesty closes fewer same-day deals than urgency theater in the short run
cons.example: a think-it-over prospect lost to a competitor's tonight-only discount that a staged-urgency script would have matched

failure_modes: promising capabilities or pricing the contract does not contain
improvising system design at the table instead of handing off to the survey discipline
acceptance_tests: the consultation runbook shows disclosure of price, term, renewal and cancellation before the close step, and every signed pack includes a rep-recorded promise summary for welcome-call verification
revisit_triggers: welcome-call mismatches or early cancellations trace to consultation conduct
the offer, contract or disclosure requirements change

nodes.definition: Design rep compensation so the person who creates an account carries a share of its early-life risk, because comp design is the strongest behavioral lever the dealer owns. The mechanism menu: an upfront commission portion paid at funding for motivation, a deferred portion vesting as the account clears the chargeback window, chargeback pass-through that reverses commission when the account claws back, and quality kickers for accounts that verify cleanly and survive. A plan that pays everything upfront transmits all cancellation risk to the dealer and quietly rewards whoever can get any signature by any means; a plan vested against the guarantee window makes the rep a partner in account quality. Two hard rules ride on top: confirmed misrepresentation forfeits the commission regardless of whether the account survives, and the plan's arithmetic is published to reps in writing so vesting never becomes a trust dispute.

included: upfront/deferred split and vesting against the guarantee window
chargeback pass-through and misrepresentation forfeiture
written plan transparency to reps
excluded: employment-law classification of reps — flagged for professional verification
asserting typical commission amounts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: guarantee-window changes, rep chargeback data or recruiting failures force a re-split

pros.claim: Vesting against the chargeback window makes the rep police their own account quality better than any manager audit
pros.example: a rep declining to write a wobbly customer because the deferred half of their commission dies with the account

cons.claim: Deferred-heavy plans lose recruits to competitors paying everything upfront
cons.example: an experienced canvasser choosing the rival's all-upfront plan despite knowing its accounts churn

failure_modes: paying all comp at signature and wondering why verification failures cluster
clawing back commissions under terms never published to the rep
acceptance_tests: the written plan shows the upfront/deferred split, vesting schedule against the agreement's actual window, chargeback pass-through and misrepresentation forfeiture, and every rep has acknowledged it before selling
revisit_triggers: the agreement's guarantee window changes
rep-level chargeback concentration or recruiting outcomes shift

nodes.definition: Assemble, for every created account, the package that makes it fundable or sellable: the signed monitoring agreement with all disclosure formalities executed (initials on renewal and term lines, cooling-off notice delivered in the required form), the qualification record with credit consent and outcome, the installation-completion and activation confirmation received from the install discipline, and the completed welcome call verifying — customer on the record — price, term, cancellation understanding and satisfaction with what was installed. Programs and account buyers fund against this package, and a defect anywhere (a missing initial, an unverified activation, a welcome call that surfaces a promise mismatch) delays funding, reprices the account or bounces it from a tranche. The package is therefore built to a checklist at creation time, not reconstructed under deadline when a funding submission looms.

included: package contents checklist
welcome-call execution and mismatch handling
defect detection before submission
excluded: performing the installation and its tests
the funding decision itself, which belongs to the program or buyer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: funder requirement changes or kickback patterns alter the checklist

pros.claim: A checklist-built package at creation time converts funding from a negotiation into a formality
pros.example: a monthly tranche accepted without a single kickback because every file passed the same internal checklist the buyer's auditors use

cons.claim: Package discipline adds administrative load to every sale, felt hardest in the smallest crews
cons.example: an owner-operator spending evenings on file completeness instead of tomorrow's appointments

failure_modes: submitting packages with missing formalities and financing the resubmission delay
treating the welcome call as a formality and missing the misrepresentation it exists to catch
acceptance_tests: every account reaches submission with agreement formalities, qualification record, activation confirmation and completed welcome call verified against the checklist, and welcome-call mismatches route back through resolution before funding
revisit_triggers: a funder changes package requirements
defect patterns appear in kickbacks or delayed fundings

nodes.definition: Manage the brutal cash shape of subsidized account creation: money leaves first — equipment purchased, installer paid, commission advanced, marketing spent — and returns later as funding after package acceptance, minus the holdback that returns latest of all or never. Map the cycle explicitly: days from sale to install, install to package completion, submission to funding, funding to holdback release, and the chargeback tail that can pull cash back after all of it. Growth multiplies the gap — every additional install per week widens the cash trough before it deepens the eventual stream — so pace is a solvency decision: the install calendar is capped by what the runway absorbs at the modeled cycle, with pre-agreed relief valves (slow installs, sell a larger tranche, shallow the subsidy) chosen in advance rather than improvised at a missed payroll. The classic dealer death is not bad accounts; it is good accounts created faster than their funding returns.

included: the mapped cash cycle from spend to holdback release
pace-versus-runway capping of the install calendar
pre-agreed relief valves for cash stress
excluded: bank or investor financing structuring — flagged for professional advice
the book's long-run cash yield after the creation phase

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured cycle durations or runway readings breach the pacing assumptions

pros.claim: An explicitly mapped cycle converts growth from an act of faith into an arithmetic pace decision
pros.example: the cycle map showing exactly how many weekly installs the current runway can carry before a tranche sale becomes necessary

cons.claim: Cash-capped pacing deliberately leaves demand unserved and can concede momentum to a better-capitalized rival
cons.example: capping installs during the summer selling peak while a funded competitor staffs up across the same streets

failure_modes: scaling installs to demand while funding lags quietly hollow out the runway
meeting a cash crunch with a panic tranche sale on the buyer's terms
acceptance_tests: a current cycle map with measured stage durations exists, the install calendar's cap traces to runway arithmetic, and the relief-valve order is written before it is needed
revisit_triggers: any cycle stage lengthens or funding terms change
runway crosses a pre-set threshold

nodes.definition: Gate every created account with a definition-of-done before it is funded, sold or handed to the monitoring book: the customer was sold under the ethics code with no open misrepresentation flag; qualification passed and is documented; the contract carries honest, jurisdiction-verified terms; the package is complete with a clean welcome call; and activation is confirmed by the install discipline. Accounts failing any condition are held with the failed condition named — resolved and re-gated, or unwound honestly — never pushed into a funding tranche to make a month-end number, because a defective account funded today returns as a chargeback, a complaint or a regulator letter with interest. The gate is also the handoff seam of this KB: what passes goes forward to installation completion and into monitoring and retention as a clean asset with its file intact.

included: the pass conditions and hold-with-reason handling
unwind decision for irreparable accounts
clean handoff into install completion and the monitoring book
excluded: retention management after handoff
the install test protocol itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: gate-failure clustering or a requirement change alters the pass conditions

pros.claim: A hard gate converts quality from an aspiration into the only path an account can travel to money
pros.example: a month-end tranche going out one account short because a welcome call surfaced a promise mismatch that had to be resolved first

cons.claim: Strict gating delays revenue on borderline accounts that would probably have been fine
cons.example: an account held a week for a missing initial while its funding slipped into the next cycle

failure_modes: waving defective accounts into tranches under month-end pressure
unwinding failures silently instead of feeding their causes back to channels, scripts and comp
acceptance_tests: no account is funded, sold or handed to the book without passing every gate condition, and each held account carries its named failed condition and resolution path
revisit_triggers: gate-failure patterns concentrate on a cause
a funder, program or jurisdiction changes what a clean account requires

edges.why_related: the program-versus-independent decision is judged by the thesis's creation-cost and account-value lens
the per-account model operationalizes the thesis's cost-to-create versus value-created question
choosing the program path makes the dealer agreement the document whose terms must be extracted
the subsidy dial is set from the creation-cost model, not from competitor advertising
the hold-path payback calculation prices the spread against the modeled creation cost
the hold side of the sell/hold comparison is the months-to-payback the spread mechanics compute
the sell side's proceeds come from the agreement's actual multiple and holdback terms
holdback fractions, windows and chargeback triggers are extracted clauses of the signed agreement
the qualification gate exists to control the chargeback exposure the guarantee mechanics define
term length is set to what subsidy recovery in the account model honestly requires
the chosen model decides whether territory is a free choice or a contract-bounded one
segments are chosen inside the territory the density and saturation analysis selected
channel choice follows from which segments must be reached (movers via realtors, homeowners via referrals)
the consultation receives the appointments the channel portfolio produces, with channel context attached
comp vesting is structured against the agreement's actual guarantee window and chargeback terms
the signed pack and recorded promises from the consultation are the package's core contents
the qualification record with consent and outcome is a required package component
the sell/hold mix determines how much cash returns and when, which the cycle map paces against
subsidy depth sets how much cash leaves per install and therefore how wide the trough runs
the gate's pass conditions are checked against the assembled package's contents
the consultation runs inside the code's disclosure-first, no-fear-selling and vulnerable-consumer rules
channel messaging and tactics must obey the honest-risk-framing and no-fear rules, not just conversion math
canvassing and calling channels launch only after the jurisdiction's solicitation and contact rules are verified
cooling-off formalities and disclosure statutes bound what the contract form must contain per jurisdiction
the plan may never pay out on conduct the code forbids; misrepresentation forfeits commission
territory scope and exclusivity clauses in the agreement bound where the map may be drawn
every account sold for cash today forfeits the spread annuity the hold path was counting on
edges.resolution_rule: sell only the tranche the cash-runway policy requires to keep creation funded; accounts beyond that requirement default to hold so the spread asset compounds

edges.why_related: rich upfront commissions reward getting any signature by any means, pressuring the code's rules
edges.resolution_rule: the code wins unconditionally: vesting spans the chargeback window, confirmed misrepresentation forfeits commission regardless of revenue, and no bonus overrides a code violation

edges.why_related: high-volume cheap channels deliver applicants the qualification gate rejects, and volume pressure pushes to lower the gate
edges.resolution_rule: the gate holds; channels whose applicants persistently fail qualification or charge back are repriced or pruned rather than the gate being loosened

edges.why_related: deeper subsidy pushes toward longer terms and harsher cancellation clauses to protect recovery, straining honest-term limits
edges.resolution_rule: terms are fixed first within honest-disclosure and jurisdiction-verified limits; subsidy depth then adjusts to what a fair term can recover — never the reverse

edges.why_related: many dealer programs oblige account flow to the program, extinguishing the hold option the dealer may strategically want
edges.resolution_rule: the signed agreement's flow obligations govern; if holding a book is the strategic goal, that is decided at model-selection time by negotiating flow terms or staying independent, not by fighting the contract later

edges.why_related: tighter point-of-sale qualification measurably lowers chargeback incidence and holdback losses downstream
how the sale was made — disclosed and unpressured versus rushed — drives the early-cancellation events that trigger chargebacks
density and saturation directly move the drive-time and marketing components of creation cost
qualification runs at or immediately after the close and must complete before any install is scheduled
funding submission follows package completion, so package speed is a stage in the cash cycle
chargeback attributions flow back into channel scoring, repricing or pruning the channels that made them
gate failures and their named causes feed rep scorecards, vesting outcomes and retraining decisions
both are capital-allocation levers trading cash today against recurring value tomorrow — subsidy spends cash to create the annuity, selling spends the annuity to recover cash

conflict_axes.name: cash_now_vs_annuity
conflict_axes.description: Selling created accounts funds tomorrow's installs immediately, while holding them builds the recurring spread asset the business exists to own.
poles: hold accounts for the recurring spread
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set a standing mix policy from cash runway and months-to-payback, selling only what the creation engine's funding requires

conflict_axes.name: subsidy_depth_vs_creation_cost
conflict_axes.description: Deeper equipment subsidy wins more doors but raises creation cost, lengthens payback and concentrates capital in cancellable accounts.
poles: subsidize deeply to maximize account creation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the dial from the account model and cash runway, varying by segment and channel quality rather than matching competitor giveaways

conflict_axes.name: program_support_vs_independence
conflict_axes.description: A dealer program funds creation and supplies brand and buyer, but takes ownership, flow obligations, quotas and exit constraints in return.
poles: join the program for funding and brand
stay independent for ownership and freedom
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide by capital position and strategic goal, with exit and ownership clauses weighed as heavily as the headline funding terms

conflict_axes.name: growth_volume_vs_account_quality
conflict_axes.description: Quota pressure and cheap lead volume push accounts through that qualification and verification standards would hold back.
poles: hold every account to the quality gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the gates hold; fix volume problems in channels, territory and offers, never by loosening qualification or verification

conflict_axes.name: closing_urgency_vs_informed_consent
conflict_axes.description: Same-visit closes are efficient and often genuine, but urgency tactics collide with disclosure-first selling and consideration time.
poles: give the prospect time and full understanding
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: welcome a same-day signature after full disclosure, never manufacture urgency, and always grant think-it-over time when asked

conflict_axes.name: security_motivation_vs_fear_selling
conflict_axes.description: Security is bought partly on worry, so honest risk conversation sits one step from manufactured fear the code bans.
poles: motivate with the prospect's real security concerns
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: speak only to concerns the prospect raised or verifiable facts, and ban invented crime claims and danger theater outright

conflict_axes.name: rep_incentive_power_vs_risk_alignment
conflict_axes.description: All-upfront commissions recruit and motivate best but transmit every chargeback to the dealer and reward signature-at-any-cost selling.
poles: pay rich and upfront to drive volume
defer and vest to align quality
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split comp with meaningful vesting across the guarantee window and publish the arithmetic; accept slower recruiting as the price of surviving accounts

conflict_axes.name: territory_density_vs_saturation
conflict_axes.description: Tight clustering compresses creation cost, but the densest attractive areas are where every competitor's canvassers already walk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cluster where saturation reads allow, and expand contiguously so density survives the move outward

conflict_axes.name: contract_protection_vs_consumer_fairness
conflict_axes.description: Longer terms and strict cancellation clauses protect subsidy recovery but strain honest disclosure and consumer-protection limits.
poles: protect the economics with hard terms
keep terms fair, plain and compliant
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fix fair, jurisdiction-verified terms first and let subsidy depth adjust to what those terms can recover

edge_cases.description: An elderly prospect grows visibly confused about the term and monthly amount midway through the close
edge_cases.trigger: signs a vulnerable consumer is not tracking the terms being agreed to
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the close, invite a family member or trusted third party, and reschedule; the sale completes only with a third party present and understanding confirmed, or not at all

edge_cases.description: A rep pitches a 'free system' while the contract recovers the equipment through the term
edge_cases.trigger: offer language promises free equipment that the term economics contradict
edge_cases.mitigation: ban 'free' language wherever a recovery obligation exists; the quote states total of payments and term, and script audits check the claim against the contract

edge_cases.description: A customer exercises the cooling-off right after equipment is installed
edge_cases.trigger: a statutory cancellation lands inside the window after a fast install
edge_cases.mitigation: honor the cancellation immediately and completely, recover equipment professionally, and treat frequent occurrences as a sales-conduct signal, not a legal problem to engineer around

edge_cases.description: The program's chargeback window outlasts the rep's commission vesting, leaving the dealer eating a clawback for a rep already paid out and gone
edge_cases.trigger: a chargeback lands after the responsible rep's comp fully vested or the rep departed
edge_cases.mitigation: align vesting length to the agreement's actual window at plan design, and hold a departing rep's unvested balance against their open window exposure

edge_cases.description: The dealer agreement terminates and its ownership and non-solicitation clauses leave the dealer with no accounts and no right to call their own former customers
edge_cases.trigger: program termination, by either side, under exit clauses signed years earlier
edge_cases.mitigation: read and negotiate exit, ownership and non-solicit clauses before signing, with counsel; model the walk-away scenario as part of choosing the program at all

edge_cases.description: Canvassers start knocking in a city that requires solicitation permits and honors a do-not-knock registry
edge_cases.trigger: door canvassing launches in a jurisdiction whose rules were not verified
edge_cases.mitigation: gate every canvassing launch on the documented jurisdiction check; pull the crew immediately when a rule surfaces mid-campaign and cure before resuming

edge_cases.description: A cheap purchased-lead source delivers strong volume whose accounts disproportionately fail funding or cancel inside the window
edge_cases.trigger: downstream quality tracking shows a channel's accounts concentrating in the at-risk ledger
edge_cases.mitigation: reprice the channel on cost per surviving funded account and prune it if it stays underwater; never subsidize a channel with the chargeback ledger

edge_cases.description: A prospect asks for covert cameras aimed into a neighbor's yard as part of the package
edge_cases.trigger: a request falls outside defensive, lawful security for the customer's own premises
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the request plainly, explain the defensive-scope line, and offer only lawful configurations for the customer's own property; walk away if the buyer insists

edge_cases.description: A growth sprint has installs running ahead of funding receipts and the payroll date approaches uncovered
edge_cases.trigger: the cash trough of subsidized creation outruns the runway mid-sprint
edge_cases.mitigation: execute the pre-agreed relief-valve order — slow the install calendar, sell the policy tranche, shallow the subsidy — instead of improvising a distressed sale

edge_cases.description: A funding tranche is repriced because several packages miss a disclosure initial the buyer's audit checks
edge_cases.trigger: package defects surface at tranche review instead of at creation
edge_cases.mitigation: run the package checklist per account at creation time and pre-audit tranches against the buyer's known checklist before submission

edge_cases.description: A renter wants a full system in a property they do not own, on the standard multi-year term
edge_cases.trigger: premises authority and tenure do not fit the standard homeowner offer
edge_cases.mitigation: require landlord consent for attached equipment and offer the renter configuration — portable components and a commitment matched to the lease horizon — instead of forcing the homeowner term

edge_cases.description: An applicant fails the credit screen and the rep proposes routing them through a workaround financing arrangement to save the deal
edge_cases.trigger: quota pressure meets a failed qualification at the table
edge_cases.mitigation: decline with dignity and offer a genuinely affordable unsubsidized alternative if one fits; any data massaging or predatory financing routing is a code violation with comp forfeiture

workflow.description: Write the operating thesis: the three revenue components, the account as the asset, both recovery paths
workflow.gate: all three revenue components and both recovery paths are stated as mechanisms with the account named as the unit of value

workflow.description: Compare program versus independent on ownership, funding, obligations and exit against the dealer's capital and goal
workflow.gate: the memo records the four-way comparison and the reason the chosen model fits capital position and strategy

workflow.description: Pull purchase mechanism, holdback, chargeback window, quotas, territory, brand rules and exit clauses from the signed document
workflow.artifact: agreement term sheet with clause references
workflow.gate: every economic and control term on the sheet traces to a clause; no folklore numbers appear anywhere

workflow.action: Set the ethics code and regulatory perimeter
workflow.description: Write and enforce the disclosure-first, no-fear-selling, vulnerable-consumer code and the per-jurisdiction obligation checklist
workflow.artifact: signed selling code and jurisdiction verification checklist
workflow.gate: banned tactics, disclosure sequence, stop-and-slow protocol and the defensive-scope line are written, and each active jurisdiction has a dated verification record

workflow.description: Compute creation cost from actual channel, comp, equipment and fee inputs and price both recovery paths
workflow.gate: creation cost computes from the dealer's own inputs and both recovery paths use only agreement-traceable terms

workflow.action: Set subsidy, pricing and contract-term architecture
workflow.description: Fix fair, jurisdiction-verified terms first, then set subsidy depth to what those terms honestly recover
workflow.artifact: offer sheet and contract form set
workflow.gate: every offer's subsidy is justified in the model and every form disclosed total of payments, term, renewal and cancellation plainly

workflow.description: Choose the clustered territory inside agreement lines and the segments with qualification criteria and matched offers
workflow.artifact: territory and segment map with qualification criteria
workflow.gate: density rationale, saturation read, agreement-rights check and per-segment offer fit are documented

workflow.description: Launch the channel portfolio with per-channel compliance checks and dual cost/quality ledgers
workflow.artifact: channel plan with compliance records and scoring ledgers
workflow.gate: every live channel has a documented jurisdiction check and a funded-cost and downstream-quality ledger

workflow.action: Run the in-home process with qualification
workflow.description: Execute the disclosure-first consultation and complete qualification before any install is scheduled
workflow.artifact: consultation runbook and signed-pack template with promise record
workflow.gate: disclosure precedes every close, and no install is scheduled before the qualification record completes

workflow.action: Design and publish the comp plan
workflow.description: Split comp across funding and vesting against the actual guarantee window with misrepresentation forfeiture
workflow.artifact: written comp plan acknowledged by every rep
workflow.gate: vesting spans the agreement's window, chargeback pass-through and forfeiture are explicit, and every rep has signed

workflow.description: Build each account's fundable package at creation time and run the welcome call against the promise record
workflow.gate: agreement formalities, qualification record, activation confirmation and a clean welcome call are checklist-verified per account

workflow.action: Gate accounts and execute the sell/hold mix
workflow.description: Pass only definition-of-done accounts into funding tranches or the held book; hold failures with named reasons
workflow.artifact: gated tranche submissions and held-book handoff records
workflow.gate: no account is funded, sold or handed off without passing all conditions, and the tranche follows the standing mix policy

priority_rationale: The frame nodes (business thesis, channel model, agreement diligence, ethics code, regulatory perimeter) come first because every economic and sales decision runs on the thesis's lens, the chosen model's terms, and the ethical and legal rails; the account-economics nodes then price creation, subsidy, spread, sell/hold and guarantee exposure before any market motion; territory, segments and the lead engine aim the machine; the selling nodes convert leads inside the code and contract architecture; and package assembly, cash pacing and the creation quality gate come last because they compose everything upstream into funded, verified accounts that hand off cleanly to installation and the monitoring book.

dominance_rules.rule: The ethical-selling code dominates every quota, tactic and incentive
dominance_rules.rationale: one pressure-sold vulnerable customer costs more in chargebacks, complaints and reputation than any month's volume gains
dominance_rules.trigger: any conflict between a closing or volume tactic and the code's disclosure, no-fear or vulnerable-consumer rules
dominance_rules.action: drop the tactic, slow or stop the sale, and audit the script that produced the conflict

dominance_rules.rule: The defensive-lawful-scope line dominates revenue on any request
dominance_rules.rationale: the business sells intrusion prevention, detection and alarm; unlawful or covert surveillance work is out of scope at any price
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect requests covert, unlawful or third-party-targeting capability
dominance_rules.action: decline plainly, offer only lawful defensive configurations, and walk away if the buyer insists

dominance_rules.rule: Honest, jurisdiction-verified contract terms dominate subsidy recovery
dominance_rules.rationale: terms that survive disclosure and local law are the only durable protection; recovery stretched through hidden terms returns as cancellations and complaints
dominance_rules.trigger: subsidy depth pressures term length, renewal or cancellation clauses past fair-and-verified limits
dominance_rules.action: hold the terms and shallow the subsidy until the fair term recovers it

dominance_rules.rule: The signed agreement dominates industry folklore on every economic term
dominance_rules.rationale: multiples, holdbacks and windows differ by contract and amendment; remembered typicals are hypotheses, not inputs
dominance_rules.trigger: any model, decision or negotiation is about to use an unverified economic term
dominance_rules.action: extract the term from the governing document (or mark the decision blocked) before proceeding

dominance_rules.rule: The quality gates dominate month-end and quota pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: a defective account funded today returns as a chargeback, complaint or regulator letter with interest
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to pass an account that fails qualification, package or gate conditions
dominance_rules.action: hold the account with its named failed condition; fix volume problems upstream in channels and offers

dominance_rules.rule: Cash-runway arithmetic dominates growth appetite in pacing
dominance_rules.rationale: subsidized creation consumes cash before funding returns it, and the classic dealer failure is growing faster than the cycle repays
dominance_rules.trigger: the install calendar's demand exceeds what the mapped cycle and runway absorb
dominance_rules.action: cap installs at the runway-derived pace and execute the pre-agreed relief valves in order

dominance_rules.rule: Verify-locally dominates any assumption about sales-side rules
dominance_rules.rationale: solicitation, cooling-off and disclosure rules differ by state and city and change; a stale assumption is an enforcement event waiting
dominance_rules.trigger: a channel, script or contract form is about to go live in any jurisdiction
dominance_rules.action: run and document the obligation-class verification before launch; block the launch until it completes

dominance_rules.rule: Mechanism honesty dominates numeric confidence in all outputs
dominance_rules.rationale: asserted commissions, multiples or rates that were never verified mislead decisions and third parties alike
dominance_rules.trigger: any output is about to state a specific economic figure as fact
dominance_rules.action: restate it as the mechanism plus where to verify the current per-deal value

dominance_rules.rule: The standing sell/hold policy dominates ad-hoc account-sale urges
dominance_rules.rationale: panic tranches sell at the buyer's price; the policy sells at the model's price
dominance_rules.trigger: a cash event or an attractive-sounding offer tempts an off-policy account sale
dominance_rules.action: route the decision through the policy's runway triggers and net-of-holdback arithmetic before any commitment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Extract the dealer agreement's actual terms before building the account model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: remodeling all economics when real holdback, multiple and window terms turn out to differ from the assumed ones

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the ethics code and verify jurisdiction rules before launching any lead channel
anti_rework_rules.prevents: dismantling and re-training a live canvassing or calling operation that launched non-compliant

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model creation cost before setting subsidy depth or matching a competitor's offer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repricing every active offer after the cash trough reveals the subsidy was uncoverable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Align comp vesting to the chargeback window when the plan is designed, not after the first clawback
anti_rework_rules.prevents: chasing departed reps for commissions on charged-back accounts and renegotiating comp mid-year

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete qualification before scheduling any install
anti_rework_rules.prevents: truck rolls, wall holes and equipment recoveries on accounts that were never fundable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build each account's package at creation time against the checklist
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing files under tranche deadline and financing the delay of kicked-back submissions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the sell/hold policy and its runway triggers before signing any agreement with account-flow obligations
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering the strategic hold option was contracted away and fighting the agreement after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Script total-of-payments, term, renewal and cancellation disclosure into the presentation before the first sale
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-papering contracts, welcome-call failures and cancellation waves from customers who learn their terms later

iteration_protocol.trigger: the chargeback rate rises or a funding tranche is repriced
iteration_protocol.action: attribute each event to channel, rep, offer and script causes; retighten the implicated gate and prune or reprice the implicated channel

iteration_protocol.trigger: the program amends multiples, holdback, window, quota or territory terms
iteration_protocol.action: re-extract the term sheet, re-run the account model and revisit the sell/hold policy against the new terms

iteration_protocol.trigger: cash runway crosses a pacing threshold
iteration_protocol.action: execute the relief-valve order — slow installs, sell the policy tranche, shallow the subsidy — and re-map the cycle

iteration_protocol.trigger: a channel's cost per funded account or downstream quality drifts past its band
iteration_protocol.action: reprice or prune the channel and reallocate spend toward surviving-account channels

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint, cancellation cluster or regulator inquiry implicates sales conduct
iteration_protocol.action: audit scripts and rep behavior against the code, retrain or remove, and check whether comp incentives fed the conduct

iteration_protocol.trigger: a sales-side rule changes in an active jurisdiction or a new jurisdiction is entered
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the obligation-class verification and update contracts, scripts and channel practices before continuing there

iteration_protocol.trigger: territory close rates fall or per-account costs rise toward saturation signals
iteration_protocol.action: re-map territory and segments, expanding contiguously before adding sales heads

iteration_protocol.trigger: welcome-call mismatches concentrate on a rep, script or offer
iteration_protocol.action: trace the promise gap to its source, correct the script or offer, and apply the comp plan's misrepresentation terms where confirmed
